text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Labor chaos predicted for Toronto: Protest leaders unfazed by court rulings limiting picketing.
- Canadian cod fishery should be reopened, says government advisory panel.
- Former Canadian Defence Minister David Collenette paid $298,000 to people with little background in military.
- Ontario doctors upset about deal with government.
- Local consortium buying Toronto baseball team: C$230 million deal includes stadium.
- Theory of evolution compatible with Christianity, says the Pope.
- Royal Bank of Canada to open 78 'superstores': Retail configuration will combine services of banking, trust and investment dealer units.
- Canadian tycoon Conrad Black bids to raise stake in Southam newspaper chain to 50.1 per cent.
- Siege mentality grips Toronto on day of labour protest: Businesses take extraordinary steps.
- Economically-troubled Ontario cities offer cash rebates to new home buyers.
- Hollinger Inc. bids to lock up control of Southam newspaper chain.
- Vancouver Stock Exchange punishes junior mining company Booker Gold Explorations Ltd: Company's press release was overenthusiastic about copper-gold discovery.
